newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares strengthen, ignore govt threat.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares strengthen, ignore govt threat.

text.p: 1117 GMT - Portuguese shares opened weaker and then recovered strongly, continuing the highs seen in recent sessions, as the market ignored the government's threat to resign if parliament gave final approval to opposition proposals on local government spending. Analysts said Portugal remained on track to qualify for the European single currency from the start.
* Portuguese shares were buoyant despite the U.S. Independence Day holiday and the mixed tone in Europe, dealers said.

* Domestic institutional and small investors were responsible for much of the Lisbon market's liquidity of 14 billion escudos. "Investment funds have been quite active," one dealer said. They said the market was flush with funds because many investors had not obtained shares in the heavily oversubscribed privatisation of EDP-Electricidade de Portugal last month.
* Investors snapped up banking stocks amid optimism over the second quarter results of the sector. Shares in Banco Portugues de Investimento hit a high of 3,790 escudos.
* Other shares that hit highs included Portugal Telecom and pulp group Portucel Industrial.
